arms.description: All case agents on Sonnet, no routing
route.mjs --cascade tier, one scripted escalation to Sonnet on a failed visible (weak) check

approvals.ideaApprovedAt: N/A (existing tool, Track E; question chosen by the user 2026-10-18)

phases.smartTrimMode: enforce for fixes, off for any re-measure

deviations: smart-context-trimming cannot be loaded in a Claude Desktop app session: off in the control session.
Case agents at effort high (same as round 3, quota mode), not xhigh.
P3 arm B folder is runs/B-claude-none (provider none = rules), not B-claude-jev as listed in arms above.

Case agents: Agent tool, subagent_type haiku-case, model sonnet (arm A and none) or haiku (arm B first attempt), effort high. Prompt is a pointer to the identical prompt.txt file from run_cascade.mjs prepare, plus the work dir.
One sentence about the tool differs between arms (A: no routing tool available; B: routing already done). Forbid check on A: 0 calls matching route.mjs|run_cascade|subagent-model-router.
The work-dir scratchpad root replaced ~/.subagent-model-router to keep the prompt paths free of the tool name.
Escalation path never fired (all 12 B first attempts passed the visible check), so the one scripted escalation is untested in P3; it was smoke-tested in P2.
results.json startedAt/finishedAt are run-dir birth/modify times (approximate); usage is real transcript usage; cost is list-price estimated.
evidence/answers are the verbatim SubagentHandback messages; the evidence/texts per-arm files were not produced (the agent run has no separate what-Claude-read text).

Review (P4, Opus, closed pack; agent-review.json): both triggers of the frozen INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rule fired (Haiku passed strict first time on every case; B used +47% paired tokens with no extra passes). Verdict kept.

Price is an estimate: scripts/pricing.mjs prices Haiku at 1/20 of Sonnet, which is not verified against official prices. Sensitivity at a 1:3 ratio: B price 0.2448 USD vs A 0.6058 USD, -59.6% (still an estimate). pricing.mjs not changed.

Token arithmetic: summary tokens sum all 12 runs per arm; pairedTokens is the mean per case over the 2 repetitions, summed over the 6 paired cases, so raw = 2 x paired by construction (build_tool_report.mjs), not double counting.
Limits: 0 visible-check failures and 0 escalations in B, so the escalation path and its cost have no live evidence (a forced-fail control is needed in a later round).
Limits: the 6 wrong refs are authored, not real Haiku mistakes; the offline gate proves the checks catch planted bugs, not Haiku failure rates.
Limits: n=12 per arm; the 1/12 tolerance cannot be resolved statistically (rule-of-three upper bound on strict-fail is about 25% at 0/12).

Limits: B used 66 model turns vs 47 for A (69 vs 53 tool calls); the driver now logs route, check, escalate and grade steps per run (driver-steps.jsonl, suggestion 6), but turns still come from the transcripts, so the cause is not attributed in this round; no re-measure.
headline: Haiku passed the hidden strict check first time in all 12 cascade runs (0 escalations, 0 silent misses); all-Sonnet also 12/12. Paired tokens 439,437 to 648,395 (+47%); price -93.9% is an estimate (-59.6% at a 1:3 Haiku:Sonnet ratio). The weak-check hypothesis was not tested: the case set is too easy for Haiku.
